headline: 8 flights cancelled as Houthi attack hits Riyadh airport
summary: Two Bangladeshis killed and four in ICU following the strike on King Khalid International Airport; nearly 3,000 passengers stranded.
details: The Iran-backed Houthi armed group launched an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, marking the third such strike this week.
The attack resulted in the deaths of two Bangladeshi nationals and left four others in the ICU, according to reports.
Following the incident, airport operations were temporarily suspended, and the Saudi authorities extended the closure until Monday morning (Bangladesh time).
As a result, eight flights from Dhaka to Riyadh have been cancelled, including flights from Biman Bangladesh Airlines, US-Bangla, Saudi Airlines, and Riyadh Airways.
According to the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB), a total of 2,951 passengers have been affected by these cancellations.
The Bangladesh government has announced that the bodies of the two deceased Bangladeshis will be repatriated at state expense.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina is closely monitoring the situation of Bangladeshi citizens in Saudi Arabia.
Passengers are advised to contact their respective airlines to verify the flight status before heading to the airport.
caption:
2 Bangladeshis killed and 4 in ICU after Houthi attack on Riyadh airport. Nearly 3,000 passengers stranded as 8 flights from Dhaka are cancelled.

The Iran-backed Houthi armed group launched an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, marking the third such strike this week.

The attack resulted in the deaths of two Bangladeshi nationals and left four others in the ICU, according to reports.

Following the incident, airport operations were temporarily suspended, and the Saudi authorities extended the closure until Monday morning (Bangladesh time).

As a result, eight flights from Dhaka to Riyadh have been cancelled, including flights from Biman Bangladesh Airlines, US-Bangla, Saudi Airlines, and Riyadh Airways.

According to the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB), a total of 2,951 passengers have been affected by these cancellations.

The Bangladesh government has announced that the bodies of the two deceased Bangladeshis will be repatriated at state expense.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina is closely monitoring the situation of Bangladeshi citizens in Saudi Arabia.

Passengers are advised to contact their respective airlines to verify the flight status before heading to the airport.

headline_marked: Rooppur Nuclear Plant: [[Unit-1 begins first nuclear fission reaction]]
headline: Rooppur Nuclear Plant: Unit-1 begins first nuclear fission reaction
summary: The reactor has reached its first criticality, marking a major milestone toward electricity generation for Bangladesh's first nuclear power project.
details: Unit-1 of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant initiated its first nuclear fission reaction at approximately 3:34 PM this afternoon, marking a major milestone for Bangladesh’s first nuclear power project.

The development marks the reactor’s first criticality, which is the point at which it reaches a stable critical state at minimum thermal power and sustains a nuclear chain reaction for the first time.
The process began after the plant received regulatory approval from the Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority (BAERA), which issued a B-2 commissioning licence last Thursday.
Project officials stated that engineers are closely monitoring reactor parameters, safety systems, and control equipment throughout the process.
The physical start-up phase, including first criticality, is expected to take about 30 to 40 days, after which power generation will be increased gradually based on test results.

Dr Md Zahedul Hassan, managing director of Nuclear Power Plant Company Bangladesh Ltd, explained that heat produced through nuclear fission will convert water into high-pressure steam to drive turbines and produce electricity.
Further regulatory approvals will be required after the successful completion of the B-2 stage before power generation can officially begin.
caption:
Bangladesh's first nuclear power plant has just reached its first criticality!

Unit-1 of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant initiated its first nuclear fission reaction at approximately 3:34 PM this afternoon, marking a major milestone for Bangladesh’s first nuclear power project.

The development marks the reactor’s first criticality, which is the point at which it reaches a stable critical state at minimum thermal power and sustains a nuclear chain reaction for the first time.

The process began after the plant received regulatory approval from the Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority (BAERA), which issued a B-2 commissioning licence last Thursday.

Project officials stated that engineers are closely monitoring reactor parameters, safety systems, and control equipment throughout the process.

The physical start-up phase, including first criticality, is expected to take about 30 to 40 days, after which power generation will be increased gradually based on test results.

Dr Md Zahedul Hassan, managing director of Nuclear Power Plant Company Bangladesh Ltd, explained that heat produced through nuclear fission will convert water into high-pressure steam to drive turbines and produce electricity.

Further regulatory approvals will be required after the successful completion of the B-2 stage before power generation can officially begin.
